title: R54 decision gate: precision mix (FP8 vs bf16 head) x batch size on RTX 5090
protocol: d12, seq=1024, graph replay + AdamW outside graph, 3-step parameter parity (all runs: 0.0), median of 20 replays; FLOPs/token = 423.9 MFLOP (3x forward).

fp8_head_b24_b48.note: invalid as fp8: fused_ce_head_v3 asserts TP*V < 2**31 (TP*V = 3.18e9 at b=24), install() silently fell back to the bf16 head; measured 126.18/165.60/247.82 ms = the bf16 numbers within 0.4%.

component_census_b16_fp8_head.note: device = 57.63 ms; residual tail (projections/gate/shared expert/norm/rope/copies/sort/fill) is derived by subtraction of the named groups.

conclusions: R50's fp8-head mix reproduces at b=16 (61.12 ms here vs 60.43 ms best on another host; same-session comparisons are the valid ones).

Reverting the FP8 head to bf16 gives 86.32 ms (+25.2 ms) and 38.41% discounted MFU - only +3.2pp over the current mix's 35.18% - because the bf16 head path runs at ~60% of bf16 peak, not at peak. It is not a cheap hedge for the discounted-MFU target.

Batch scaling cannot reach 60% either: b>=24 FP8 silently falls back (int32 TP*V limit), and the all-bf16 b=16/24/32/48 points fit ~5.0 ms per 1k tokens, i.e. ~41% discounted asymptote. This is consistent with the earlier marginal analysis (~42% asymptote for the current mix).

Discounted 60% = 35.83 ms at b=16; from 61.03 ms it needs -25.2 ms and therefore a component-level program (head -2.2, MoE -3.5~-4.5 via grouped FP8, attention -2.5~-4, mHC -4.5~-5.5, tail/other -6~-9, gap -1) - only if every floor lands (34-41 ms => 58-69%).
Fix applied: fused_ce_head_v3 now warns once when it silently falls back to the bf16 head, and its docstring documents the TP*V < 2**31 limit.
